name: prefers-color-scheme
plain: Whether the OS or browser theme is light or dark.
meaning: Reveals the person's OS appearance setting (dark mode is used by an estimated 40 to 60% of mobile users) and time of day if auto switching. Low entropy; often set at the site by cookie.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

limits.headline: Can tell whether your device theme is light or dark
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads.
can: Check whether you chose light or dark
Ask for it in a request header, in Chrome, once the site opts in
cannot: See your wallpaper or other theme colors

story.what_it_is: Tells a page whether your device is set to a light or dark theme.

marketing.name: prefers-color-scheme
marketing.pitch: Google teaches sites to follow the system dark or light setting so pages feel native and ease eye strain.

marketing.name: prefers-color-scheme
marketing.pitch: Documents the media feature that tells a page if the person wants a light or dark theme.

story.for_you: You never see the check, but you see the result. If your phone is in dark mode, many sites open dark without you doing a thing.
story.for_makers: Matching dark mode makes a site feel polished and avoids a bright flash at night. It also leaks a tiny fact about you. Together with other signals it helps tell your devices apart.

use_cases.example: A social feed opens in dark colors in the evening because your phone is in dark mode.
A browser game offers a dark menu that matches your system so it is easy on the eyes during late sessions.
A news or reading site switches to light text on dark for night reading.
A document or code editor switches theme when your system goes dark at sunset.
An advertiser serves a dark version of a banner so it does not glare against a dark page.
A team sees that 60 percent of evening visitors use dark mode and tests a darker design.
A fingerprint script adds the theme to a list of settings to help recognise a returning browser.

legit_uses: Respect OS theme and accessibility needs
abuse: Infer disability or setting for fingerprinting
